name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do it: Build a "prompt health score" metric that rates every prompt on clarity, conciseness, and task alignment. Run it weekly on all active prompts and flag the bottom 10% for review. Trade-off: We accept false positives—some prompts will look bad but work fine—because the cost of missing a real problem is higher than the noise.

name: Gauge
text: The risk isn’t just false positives—it’s that a weekly score turns prompts into a compliance checklist, not a living tool. A better alternative: tie the score to actual task outcomes, not static reviews. Settle it by running a 2-week A/B test where we auto-flag prompts only if their scores correlate with worse task results.
